topicTitle: Profiling Memory Leaks with DevTools Snapshots

lessons.title: Locating Detached DOM Node Leaks
lessons.description: Detached DOM nodes are elements removed from the page but still referenced in JavaScript — they leak memory.

sections.heading: What are detached DOM leaks?
paragraphs: When you remove an element from the DOM but still hold a reference to it in JavaScript, the element can't be garbage collected. This is called a detached DOM leak.
list: Removed from DOM but referenced in JavaScript
Each detached node keeps its children and event listeners in memory
Common in SPAs where elements are created and removed frequently
Use DevTools Memory tab to identify them

codeExamples.heading: Creating and finding detached nodes
explanation: When div is removed from the DOM, it becomes 'detached'.
leakedElements still holds a reference — the node can't be garbage collected.
Clear the reference to allow garbage collection.
DevTools Memory snapshots show detached nodes as memory leaks.

practice.task: Create a function that adds and removes DOM elements, keeping references to removed ones. Use DevTools to take heap snapshots and identify the detached nodes.
hints: Add elements to the DOM and push to an array.
Remove from DOM but keep in array.
Take heap snapshot and filter by 'Detached' elements.

keyTakeaways: Detached DOM nodes are removed from the page but still referenced in JavaScript.
They keep themselves and their children in memory — a common leak source.
Clear references when removing elements to allow garbage collection.
DevTools Memory tab heap snapshots identify detached nodes.
lessons.challenge: Find and fix a detached DOM leak in a todo list app that creates and removes items.

lessons.title: Tracing Retained Closure Scope Leaks
lessons.description: Closures can unintentionally retain large objects in their scope — a subtle but serious memory leak.

sections.heading: Closure memory leaks
paragraphs: A closure retains everything in its enclosing scope, even variables it doesn't use. If a closure references a large object, that object stays in memory as long as the closure exists.
list: Closures retain the entire enclosing scope
Unused variables in the scope are still retained
Long-lived closures with large scope = memory leak
Use DevTools to check retained objects in closure scope

codeExamples.heading: Closure scope leak
explanation: The increment closure retains the entire processData scope, including hugeData.
Even though increment doesn't use hugeData, it's still in memory.
Setting hugeData to null explicitly releases it from the closure scope.
DevTools Memory snapshots show retained objects in closure scope.

practice.task: Create a closure that retains a large array unnecessarily. Use DevTools to identify the retained object. Then fix it by releasing the reference.
hints: Create a function with a large local variable.
Return a closure that doesn't use the large variable.
Check DevTools Memory → Closure section in heap snapshot.

keyTakeaways: Closures retain the entire enclosing scope — even unused variables.
Large objects in closure scope can't be garbage collected while the closure lives.
Explicitly null out references you no longer need.
DevTools Memory snapshots show what closures retain.
lessons.challenge: Build a pub/sub system that cleans up event listeners and closures when subscribers unsubscribe.

lessons.title: Heap Snapshot Analysis & Allocation Timelines
lessons.description: Use DevTools to take heap snapshots, compare them and track memory allocation over time.

sections.heading: Using DevTools Memory tab
list: Heap Snapshot — captures all objects in memory at a point in time
Allocation Timeline — shows memory allocation over time
Compare snapshots to find objects that are growing or not being freed

codeExamples.heading: Heap snapshot workflow
explanation: Take a snapshot before and after the action to compare.
The Comparison view shows objects added between snapshots.
Filter by 'Detached' to find DOM elements removed from the page.
The Retainers panel shows what's preventing garbage collection.

practice.task: Use Chrome DevTools to take 3 heap snapshots: before, during and after creating 1000 DOM elements. Compare the snapshots to verify elements are properly cleaned up.
hints: Compare snapshots 1 and 3 to verify cleanup.

keyTakeaways: Heap snapshots capture all objects in memory at a point in time.
Compare snapshots to find objects that persist unexpectedly.
The Retainers panel shows what's preventing garbage collection.
Allocation Timeline tracks memory usage over time for real-time leak detection.
lessons.challenge: Profile a single-page application and identify the top 3 sources of memory growth over a 5-minute session.
